we have created a tunable narrow-passband waveguide that permits the transmission at one, both or none of two selected frequencies and we have created a Y shaped waveguide that permits multiplexing and/or demultiplexing of waves at two selected frequencies.
waveguides composed by a row of hollow steel cylinders in a phononic crystal can have a tunable NPB located in the band gap of the crystal.
the wave propagation characteristics of phononic crystals with filled and hollow cylinders can be controlled by changing the inner radius and filling of the hollow cylinders.

the design of tunable waveguides and demultiplexers for acoustic waves in the MHz regime.
a new class of phononic crystals that exhibit a tunable NPB and that can be used as a frequency selective device for the transport and demultiplexation of acoustic waves.
the development of acoustic band gap (ABGs) materials with tunable narrow pass bands (NPB's) and the use of these materials in the design of tunable filters and demultiplexers for acoustic waves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown the existence of tunable narrow pass bands (NPB) in waveguides made of a row of steel hollow cylinders in water.
the use of hollow cylinders in 2D ABG materials is very promising for the design of acoustic devices with tunable and selective filtering and multiplexing capabilities.

the present work demonstrates that waveguides constituted by hollow cylinders in 2D phononic crystals can exhibit NPB's that can be tuned by adjusting the inner radii of the hollow cylinders, by changing the nature and/or the density of the fluid that they contain, or by a combination of both methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the NPB's of ABG waveguides can be tuned by changing the inner radius of their hollow cylinders and by changing the nature that fills them.
the use of hollow cylinders can provide a new way of controlling the propagation of acoustic waves in phononic crystals.
the use of hollow cylinders in ABG materials can be used to create devices that can be used for filtering and demultiplexer of acoustic waves.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the properties of waveguide made of hollow cylinders are very sensitive to their internal fluid.
waveguides constituted by hollow cylinders in 2D phononic crystals can be used as tunable narrow band filters, as frequency selective waveguides, and as frequency demultiplexers.
the NPB's of ABG materials with hollow cylinders are tunable and can be used for the filtering and multiplexing of sound.
